QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_23

question.text: 1-day 95% VaR of a Cat III fund = INR 4 crore. Scale to a 10-day holding-period VaR (assume iid returns, √T scaling).

explanation.text: The Logic: VaR is a downside-risk measure over a stated time frame and confidence level. Applying the square-root-of-time scaling supplied in the stem: 10-day VaR = 1-day VaR × √10 = 4 × 3.1623 = INR 12.65 crore. The Trap: INR 40 crore multiplies by 10 (no square root). INR 8.94 crore uses √5 instead of √10. INR 4 crore ignores scaling entirely. Note: The √T scaling assumption is given in the stem (iid returns); it is not itself a rule from the workbook.
